samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copy carries comment threads for sheet/slides/board, contradicting the documented "comments are not carried over" contract and diverging from the doc/pdf copy paths
samples.evidence: Sheet comments live inside the copied Yorkie root: `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:94` declares `Worksheet.comments: { [threadId]: Thread }`, seeded at creation (`:147`), and the frontend reads/writes them there (`packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1318`, `:1366`). `DocumentCopyService.copyContent` copies every root key verbatim for `JSON_ROOT_TYPES = ['sheet','slides','board']` (packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts, the `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(snapshot))` write), so `root.sheets[tabId].comments` — other users' threads, authors, bodies, resolved state — is duplicated into the new document. The `doc` path (readDocsRoot/writeDocsRoot) and the pdf path do NOT carry comments (`packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:24` shows docs comments live at `root.comments`, which `readDocsRoot` ignores). Both the service header comment and `docs/design/document-copy.md:33` state "Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over". Either the sheet snapshot must strip `sheets[*].comments` or the contract must be corrected.

samples.summary: Bulk "Make a copy" issues one HTTP request per document against the global 120 req/min throttle bucket, so a large selection 429s partway and reports a single generic failure
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:98` configures a single global throttler bucket `{ ttl: 60_000, limit: 120 }` shared by every route (the comment there notes named throttlers stack, so this is the ceiling for all non-overridden routes; `documents/:id/copy` adds no `@Throttle` override). The new frontend mutation loops sequentially: `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-list.tsx:564` `for (const id of ids) await copyDocument(id);`. Selecting >120 documents (or fewer, since list refetches and other API calls share the bucket) makes the tail of the loop 429; the mutation surfaces only `toast.error("Failed to copy")` with no indication of which copies succeeded. Bulk move/delete avoid this by using single atomic endpoints (`@Patch('documents/move')`, `@Post('documents/delete')`).

samples.summary: Copied CRDT documents still share embedded image objects with the source, so the copy is not fully "independent" as the service doc claims
samples.evidence: Images embedded in sheets/board/slides/docs are uploaded to object storage and referenced by URL inside the Yorkie root (`packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:34-45` `SheetImage.src`; uploaded via `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:36` to `/api/v1/workspaces/:id/images`). `DocumentCopyService` copies only the `Document.fileId` blob (`FileService.copy`) and leaves these embedded image keys shared between source and copy. The service header states "Both blob and CRDT paths produce an *independent* copy — deleting the source (which deletes its blob) cannot affect it", which does not hold for embedded images if anything ever deletes them (`packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts:79` and `packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:99` expose DELETE endpoints). I found no caller of those DELETE endpoints in the frontend, so today the exposure is limited to the doc comment being overstated; confirming would need a check of the CLI/any cleanup job for image deletion.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. document-copy.service.ts:176-198 copies every root key verbatim for types 'sheet'|'slides'|'board' (JSON_ROOT_TYPES at :27; snapshot via snapshotJsonRoot :209-220; write loop :192-194) with no filtering. Sheet comment threads are stored inside that same root: worksheet-document.ts:94-96 declares Worksheet.comments keyed by threadId, seeded at :147, and sheets is a root field (:118); the frontend reads/writes them there (yorkie-store.ts:1318, :1327, :1366). So root.sheets[*].comments — other users' threads, authors, bodies, resolved state — is duplicated into the copy. The other arms genuinely do not carry comments: readDocsRoot (docs-tree.ts:427-468) reads only content/pageSetup/stylesJson and ignores root.comments where docs comments live (docs-document.ts:24, :49), and the blob path copies bytes only. This directly contradicts the stated contract in the service header (document-copy.service.ts:34-37) and docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35 ("Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over"), while :88 of the design doc describes the very mechanism that picks comments up. No guard strips comments anywhere, and no spec test covers it (document-copy.service.spec.ts has no 'comments' reference). In-lane for blast radius: the defect is only visible by leaving the diff to read the sheets model and frontend store that own the comments sub-tree; it is a cross-module invariant/contract violation with real impact (collaboration state leaking into a new document). No refutation ground applies.
